prompt: A mid-size consumer electronics company is considering entering a new international market. Identify the top 3 risks using the data given, and the single risk that should be resolved before any other planning proceeds.
context: Market research (commissioned, internal) shows a large addressable market and receptive consumer sentiment. Legal counsel has flagged that the target country requires a local joint-venture partner holding at least 30% ownership for the company's product category, and that finding a suitable, trustworthy partner has historically taken competitors 9-18 months. Currency has been volatile (a named 22% depreciation against the dollar in the last 18 months, per public FX data). Two named competitors already operate in-market with an estimated combined 45% share.

binaryCriteria.description: Identifies the mandatory local joint-venture partner requirement as the risk that must be resolved before any other planning proceeds, since it is a legal precondition, not a discretionary consideration.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the JV requirement is treated as just one risk among several rather than the gating precondition.

binaryCriteria.description: Names currency volatility and competitive intensity as material risks to the economics/strategy, while distinguishing them from the gating JV-partner risk.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if these risks are omitted entirely, or are ranked above the JV requirement as the top priority.

binaryCriteria.description: References the 9-18 month historical lead time for finding a JV partner when explaining why this risk must be addressed first / why it affects the overall entry timeline.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the answer does not connect the JV search timeline to the overall market-entry planning horizon.

goldNotes: A strong answer identifies the mandatory joint-venture partner requirement as the risk that must be resolved before any other market-entry planning proceeds — it is a legal precondition (not just a business preference) and has a long, uncertain lead time (9-18 months per the given precedent), meaning it gates the entire timeline. Currency volatility (22% depreciation) and competitive intensity (45% combined share held by 2 incumbents) are real risks but are not gating preconditions — they affect the economics and go-to-market strategy, not whether entry is legally possible at all. A weak answer treats all risks as equally prioritized, or picks currency/competition as the "must resolve first" risk instead of the structural JV requirement.
